runs.content: Carnival (NYSE, $25.76) was bought as the day's earnings-catalyst pick. Its 09-29 Q3 beat (EPS $1.43 vs $1.35) raised FY26 EPS guidance to $2.24 on record yields and deposits, yet the stock trades ~11.5x that guidance and 24% below its 52-week high, and it adds travel/leisure exposure to a healthcare- and energy-heavy book. ICE was exited as a capacity trim (−6.57%, −$66; weakest position, no thesis break). No stop/T1/T2 triggers; RIGL is $3.17 from T1 and HPQ is $5.40 from T2. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,156 (+1.61% on $72,000).

Target (NYSE, $156.70) was bought as the day's momentum pick. It holds a +24% 3-month uptrend near its 52-week high at only ~16x earnings, and the Fiddelke turnaround is showing up in traffic-led comps (Q2 +3.8% vs a 2.4% estimate, FY sales guide raised to ~5%). It also diversifies the book away from healthcare. HUM was exited as a capacity trim (−8.63%, −$86); it was the weakest position and its momentum thesis had broken. No stop/T1/T2 triggers; HPQ is $5.37 from T2 and RIGL is $3.36 from T1. Portfolio net P&L: +$1,118 (+1.57% on $71,000).
